messages:
sri: FYI customer ACME reported a big drop in embeddings vectors/sec starting at ~11:12 UTC after yesterday's routing rollout. Tokens/sec looks steady but vecs/sec down ~55%. They're seeing 429s and higher tail latency. Putting notes + repro below.

oliver: thanks — can you paste the minimal request they used and any metrics you have? particularly GPU queue depth and per-model slot utilization.

sri: customer payload (redacted API key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-compact-v2","input":["doc1","doc2",...],"batch_size":64}'
```
Metrics snapshot around 11:12: tokens_per_sec: 1200 (stable), vectors_per_sec: 540 -> 240, gpu_queue_depth: spiking to 850, model_slots_used: 98%, kvcache_lock_waits:+1200/s. Also saw a flurry of 429 auth errors from billing validation service: `auth-service: 429 rate_limit` (followed by client retries).

mara: sounds like a dependent-service (billing/auth) retry storm is backing up front-end workers and reducing effective batch formation -> smaller batches hitting heavy quantized path -> lower vecs/sec. Could also be dim fallback if some inputs force a different variant. Any dim mismatch logs?

sri: good call. Customer confirmed mixed vectors payloads — some legacy rows still sending 512-dim arrays while new model expects 768. Server logged `embedding_dimension_mismatch` and we triggered fallback to `embed-compat-512` which is single-threaded C++ path and much slower. Example log: 
```
[11:12:03] rnd-srv-17 WARN embedding_dimension_mismatch user=acme id=xyz expected=768 got=512 fallback=embed-compat-512
[11:12:04] rnd-srv-17 ERROR kvcache_lock_wait wait_ms=320 lat_p95=1.2s
```

devin: ok that explains both the dim mismatch slowdown and the backlog. But what about the 429s from auth service? Are those internal rate-limits or customer-side token bursts?

sri: support-bot forwarded customer trace: the auth-checking microservice started returning 429 for internal token-validate calls between 11:10-11:16. Looks like a deploy triggered a temporary throttle on the auth cluster; front-end retries were set to aggressive (exponential backoff with max 8 retries) and we had many concurrent validate calls for every embed request because of stale session tokens.

arina: repro steps I used locally to emulate: 1) send mixed-dim batch (half 512, half 768) 2) throttle /validate endpoint with `tc qdisc` to 100ms and 50% drop 3) run concurrency 120 workers. Observed same drop: gpu queue depth spikes and vecs/sec halved. Minimal script: 
```python
# pseudo-repro
for i in range(120):
  requests.post('/v1/embeddings', json=mixed_batch)
```

oliver: great repro. Immediate mitigations: 1) tell customer to normalize dims (fast) 2) temporarily route ACME to `embed-compat-768` pinned variant (avoid fallback) 3) throttle front-end auth-retries to avoid retry storms 4) rollback auth deploy or increase auth cluster capacity. Any objections?

mara: +1. Also add a quick config to short-circuit dimension mismatch earlier with a 400-level response (instead of silent fallback) for enterprise accounts until they fix payloads — reduces unexpected pivot to slow path.

devin: I'll patch short-term: change retry policy for auth calls to max 2 retries with jitter and add a counter to shed requests when `gpu_queue_depth>700`. Also add an alert `vecs/sec_degraded` tied to `gpu_queue_depth` and `dim_mismatch_rate>0.1%`.

sri: I've informed customer of recommended steps and gave repro script. They're ok with being pinned while they tidy payloads. Marking this escalated -> eng-runtime for follow-up. cc @oncall (ops-bot) :thumbsup:

ops-bot: acknowledged. Created incident INC-2026-8976, assigned to devin. Logs and traces: https://r-infra/trace/3861248000/ACME

sri: thanks everyone — summary for the incident thread: mixed-dim payloads triggered fallback to slower embedding variant + auth validate retry storm due to recent deploy -> front-end backlog -> GPU queue saturation -> vecs/sec regression and 429s. Workarounds: pin variant, reduce retries, normalize dims. Followups: make dim-mismatch explicit 4xx opt-in for enterprise, improve kvcache lock metrics, add shed policy when queue depth high.
